# IFAS simulated training data

**These files are SIMULATED (synthetic) data.** They were generated by `generate_data.py` to look like the
finances of three kinds of IFAS workspaces. They are for developing and testing the system only (forecasting
model, unusual-spending detector, budget alerts, CSV import and the AI assistant). They are **not real
records and must never be reported as research findings** in Chapter 4 (data analysis) or Chapter 5.

Currency: KES. Period: 1 Nov 2023 to 31 Oct 2026 (36 months). Seed: 2026 (change `SEED` to regenerate).

## Files

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `transactions_personal.csv` | Personal workspace: salary, side income, rent, groceries, transport, utilities, education, savings and transfers |
| `transactions_business.csv` | Business workspace (a hardware shop): daily till and M-Pesa till sales, stock purchases, rent, salaries, licences, owner drawings |
| `transactions_organization.csv` | Organization workspace (a youth development fund): grants, donations, membership fees, and expenses by department |
| `anomaly_labels.csv` | Ground-truth labels for every transaction (`is_anomaly`, `anomaly_type`) for training and evaluating unusual-spending detection |
| `monthly_expense_series.csv` | Monthly expense totals by TOTAL, CATEGORY (and DEPARTMENT for the organization) for forecasting |
| `budgets.csv` | Monthly budgets (by category, or by department for the organization) for budget-alert tests |
| `accounts.csv`, `categories.csv`, `departments.csv` | Set-up data for each workspace |
| `savings_goals.csv` | Personal savings goals |
| `assistant_eval_questions.csv` | 43 test questions with expected behaviour for the AI Financial Assistant |
| `generate_data.py`, `make_eval.py` | Scripts that created the files |

## Transaction CSV layout (also the IFAS import format)

`ref, date, description, amount, type, account, to_account, category, department`

- `ref`: optional external reference (PER-/BUS-/ORG- prefix); the importer may ignore it.
- `date`: YYYY-MM-DD.
- `amount`: positive number in KES. The sign is carried by `type`.
- `type`: INCOME, EXPENSE or TRANSFER.
- `account`: the account the money leaves (expense/transfer) or enters (income).
- `to_account`: only for TRANSFER (the receiving account); empty otherwise.
- `category`: category name (`Transfers` and `Savings` are used for transfers).
- `department`: only for the organization workspace; empty otherwise.

## Other files

`anomaly_labels.csv`: `ref, workspace_type, is_anomaly (0/1), anomaly_type`.
Types: LARGE_AMOUNT, DUPLICATE, ROUND_LARGE_CASH, FREQUENCY_BURST, UNUSUAL_CATEGORY, NONE.

`monthly_expense_series.csv`: `workspace_type, level, name, month, total_expense, total_expense_excl_anomalies, txn_count`.
Use `total_expense_excl_anomalies` to train the forecaster on normal behaviour and `total_expense` to test how
anomalies affect it.

`budgets.csv`: `workspace_type, category, department, period_start, period_end, amount_limit, alert_threshold`
(threshold is the percentage of the limit at which a warning is raised).

`assistant_eval_questions.csv`: `id, workspace_type, role, question, question_type, expected_behavior,
must_include, must_not_include` (semicolon-separated checks).

## Suggested use

| Task | Training / tuning | Testing |
|---|---|---|
| Expense forecasting | First 30 months (Nov 2023 to Apr 2026) of `monthly_expense_series.csv` | Last 6 months (May to Oct 2026), chronological, never shuffled |
| Unusual-spending detection | Unlabelled transactions before 1 May 2026 (unsupervised models), or labelled rows (supervised comparison) | Transactions from 1 May 2026, scored against `anomaly_labels.csv` |
| Budget alerts | `budgets.csv` with the transactions | Check that 80% and 100% alerts are raised in the correct months |
| CSV import | The three transaction files, plus copies you damage on purpose (missing date, bad amount, duplicates) | Validation preview counts |
| AI assistant | Build `context_json` from these data | Run `assistant_eval_questions.csv` against the assistant |

## Known properties and limits

- About 4% of expense rows are injected anomalies, which is higher than in real life so that there are enough
  examples to evaluate. Real data will have fewer, and some "normal" large items.
- Category-level monthly series are noisy and sparse (some categories have no spending in some months); total
  monthly expenses are much easier to forecast. Plan for this in the interface (show accuracy, allow
  "insufficient data").
- Seasonality (December, January school costs) and about 6% yearly price growth are built in.
- Descriptions are generic. There is no time-of-day column, so "unusual timing" is represented by bursts of
  many transactions on one day.
- The data has no relationship to any real person, business or organization.
